messages:
maria: hey team — quick helm question. i'm seeing weird behavior when a parent chart sets an empty string for a key that a subchart also defines. expected subchart default to win, but rendered env var becomes an empty string instead. is empty string considered an explicit override?
kevin: yes, helm treats an explicitly set empty string as a value (not nil). if values.yaml in parent has `myservice:\n  LOG_LEVEL: \"\"` it counts as set and will override subchart defaults.
olga: short workaround: unset the key in parent or set it to `null` so the subchart default will apply. alternatively handle in template with sprig helpers.
maria: can you share a small example of the template fix? trying to avoid touching all our parent charts.
kevin: you can guard in the template, e.g.
```yaml
env:\n  - name: LOG_LEVEL\n    value: {{ if or (not .Values.myservice.LOG_LEVEL) (eq .Values.myservice.LOG_LEVEL "") }}"info"{{ else }}{{ .Values.myservice.LOG_LEVEL }}{{ end }}
```
this treats empty string as missing and falls back to "info". note `not` on a string is true if string is empty? sprig truthiness: empty string is zero value so `not` works.
sam: small nit: the above will break if the path `.Values.myservice` is nil in some installs — add full chaining to be safe: `and (hasKey .Values "myservice") .Values.myservice.LOG_LEVEL` or use `index` to avoid panics.
olga: alternate: use `default` from sprig: `{{ default "info" .Values.myservice.LOG_LEVEL }}` — `default` will return the second arg if the first is empty/nil/zero. cleaner.
maria: nice — does `default` also treat empty string as empty and fallback?
kevin: yes, default treats empty string as empty and will use the fallback. so `{{ default "info" .Values.myservice.LOG_LEVEL }}` is exactly what you want.
maria: great. follow-up: we have many nested maps and some parents pass `envFrom:` blocks via umbrella values. if a parent passes `envFrom: []` (empty list) that wipes subchart envFrom. is there a way to merge lists instead of overriding?
sam: helm values are merged by overlay: list values are replaced (not merged). there's no native deep list concat in helm. you have to implement merge logic in templates or change values structure to maps.
olga: pattern i've used: accept a map of extra env entries in the subchart and then in the parent set that map with keys you want to override. avoid list-to-list merging.
maria: can you show a compact template snippet that appends parent-provided list to default list?
kevin: you can do something like:
```gotemplate
{{- $defaults := list (dict "name" "LOG_LEVEL" "value" "info") -}}
{{- $extra := default (list) .Values.myservice.extraEnv -}}
{{- $merged := append $defaults $extra -}}
env: {{ toYaml $merged | nindent 2 }}
```
this treats extraEnv as a list in values that parent can set to add items; avoids parent zeroing out the default unless they intentionally set extraEnv to empty list.
maria: ah ok so rather than parent setting `env:` directly, they should set `extraEnv:`. i'll add a short note to the chart README and send a PR updating templates. PTAL @kevin @olga — small code changes, should be quick.
deploy-bot: CI: chart-lint job queued for maria/helm-subchart-fixes (pr #832).
kevin: pinged in the PR for review. also, if you want an automated check, we can add a helm unit test to assert fallback behavior for empty string vs null.
maria: thanks all — will open PR shortly and add a README blurb about empty vs null and the `default` helper.
sam: fwiw, in terraform-managed overlays we sometimes generate `null` vs `""` incorrectly when templating values files — watch that pipeline, might need a fix there too.
maria: noted. filing a follow-up with infra once PR is up. :thumbsup:
